title: Molecular docking, characterization, ADME/toxicity prediction, and anti-ulcer activity of new quercetin derivatives on indomethacin-induced gastric ulcer in mice.
authors: Salem, Maha B; Saleh, Abdulrahman M; Seif El-Din, Sayed H; Samir, Safia; Hammam, Olfat A; El-Lakkany, Naglaa M
one_liner_zh: 该文研究槲皮素衍生物对吲哚美辛诱导胃溃疡的分子对接与抗溃疡活性，对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Gastric ulcer (GU) is a serious upper gastrointestinal tract disorder that affects people worldwide. The drugs now available for GU treatment have a high rate of relapses and drug interactions, as well as mild to severe side effects. As a result, new natural therapeutic medications for treating GU with fewer negative side effects are desperately needed. Because of quercetin's (QCT) diverse pharmacological effects and unique structural features, we decided to semi-synthesize new QCT derivatives and test them for antiulcer activity. Docking assays were performed on the synthesized compounds to determine their affinity for TLR-4/MD-2, MyD88/TIR, and NF-kappaB domains, an important inflammatory pathway involved in GU development and progression. Mice were given oral famotidine (40 mg/kg/day), QCT, QCT pentamethyl (QPM), or QCT pentaacetyl (QPA) (50 mg/kg/day) for 5 days before GU induction by a single intraperitoneal injection of indomethacin (INDO; 18 mg/kg). QPM and QPA have a stronger binding affinity for TLR-4/MD-2, MyD88/TIR and NF-kappaB domains than QCT. In comparison, they demonstrated the greatest reduction in ulcer score and index, gastric MDA and nitric oxide (NO) contents, MyD88 and NF-kappaB expressions, and gastric TLR-4 immunostaining. They also enhanced the levels of GSH, CAT, COX-1, and COX-2 in the gastric mucosa, as well as HO-1 and Nrf2 expression, with histological regression in gastric mucosal lesions, with QPA-treated mice demonstrating the best GU healing. QPA is safe against all of the target organs and adverse pathways studied, with good ADME properties. However, further in vitro experiments are necessary to demonstrate the inhibitory effects of QPM and QPA on the protein targets of interest. In addition, preclinical research on its bioavailability and safety is essential before clinical management can be undertaken. Overall, the new QPA derivative could one day serve as the basis for a new class of potential antiulcer drugs.
abstract_zh: 胃溃疡（GU）是一种影响全球人群的严重上消化道疾病。目前用于GU治疗的药物存在复发率高、药物相互作用以及轻度至重度副作用等问题。因此，迫切需要开发副作用更少的新型天然治疗药物来治疗GU。鉴于槲皮素（QCT）多样的药理作用和独特的结构特征，我们决定半合成新的QCT衍生物并测试其抗溃疡活性。对合成的化合物进行了对接分析，以确定它们与TLR-4/MD-2、MyD88/TIR和NF-kappaB结构域的亲和力，这些是参与GU发生和发展的重要炎症通路。小鼠在通过单次腹腔注射吲哚美辛（INDO；18 mg/kg）诱导GU前，口服法莫替丁（40 mg/kg/天）、QCT、QCT五甲基化物（QPM）或QCT五乙酰化物（QPA）（50 mg/kg/天）5天。QPM和QPA对TLR-4/MD-2、MyD88/TIR和NF-kappaB结构域的结合亲和力强于QCT。相比之下，它们在溃疡评分和指数、胃黏膜MDA和一氧化氮（NO）含量、MyD88和NF-kappaB表达以及胃TLR-4免疫染色方面表现出最大程度的降低。它们还提高了胃黏膜中GSH、CAT、COX-1和COX-2的水平，以及HO-1和Nrf2的表达，并伴有胃黏膜病变的组织学消退，其中QPA处理的小鼠显示出最佳的GU愈合效果。QPA对所有研究的目标器官和不良通路均安全，且具有良好的ADME特性。然而，仍需进一步的体外实验来证明QPM和QPA对目标蛋白的抑制作用。此外，在进行临床管理之前，对其生物利用度和安全性的临床前研究至关重要。总体而言，新的QPA衍生物有朝一日可能成为一类潜在抗溃疡药物的基础。
